lecons.html:
We are obliged to live in the spiritual world at the same time as we live in this physical world. It is not possible to do without the spiritual world. Every person is constantly in contact, willingly or not, with the spiritual world. Either man is in control of his spiritual environment, or he is subject to it, but he cannot do without it. We ourselves are spiritual beings; spirits rub shoulders with us and influence us, unless we influence them. More is going on around you than you imagine. And there is no point in imagining it. You must understand the spiritual reality around you and know how to keep your spiritual environment under control.

We are not supposed to be subjected. We are supposed to be in control. God created man to rule. Admittedly, man’s rule bears more on the physical world. But since the physical world is governed by the spiritual world, our authority must rise into the spiritual realm to be effective in the physical. That is why Jesus gave us the power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the evil one (Luke 10:19). This has everything to do with the spiritual world and is so that our dominion would be effective in every area.

Wielding this spiritual power, being in control of one’s spiritual environment, managing the affairs of this life from the spiritual realm, are what we will see with the help of the Holy Spirit.

God is Spirit (John 4:24). And he is the Father of spirits (Hebrews 12:9). That is, the creator, the God of the spirits of all flesh (Numbers 27:16). He is the creator of every man and woman on our earth and he made us spirits who inhabit bodies. What is more, he created spirits without bodies, which are the angels, the demons including the devil. (Note that God did not create the devil and the demons as they are today. God made them angels with blessed tasks. But they deliberately left that good position through disobedience and rebellion, seeking to be worshiped in place of God the Creator. Everything originates from God although not all things have kept their dignity.)

The creatures that have bodies are, in this case, human beings. We are not speaking of animals, plants and the like because they do not have spirits. Animals have souls. But they have no spirit. They do, however, have a slight spiritual dimension that God conferred on them. Human beings are the only creatures of God that are spirits having souls and dwelling in physical bodies. We are both physical and spiritual beings. We can pass at any moment from one dimension to the other and we can live both dimensions at once. But the noises of the physical world and its attractions compel us to be more physically oriented. Which is, however, very dangerous.

Spirits without bodies make up the spiritual world. In other words, the spiritual world is made up of everything that the physical eye cannot naturally see, not even by means of the most sophisticated microscope. God is master in this world. He is the Father of spirits, the sovereign whose will no spirit can violate with impunity.

The attributes of God

God is Almighty. His strength has no limit. He cannot get tired. He can never run out of energy. He does not need to be recharged. He is the very source of all power. He cannot be equaled, much less surpassed. God, in matters of strength, is above everything.

God is omniscient. He knows everything. He does not need to be informed. He knows the past, the present and the future. God knows everything that is happening everywhere at the same time. God knows even the most hidden thoughts of every creature. No creature is hidden from him, but all things are naked and laid bare to the eyes of him to whom we must give account. There is no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account. (Heb 4:13)

God is omnipresent. He neither goes nor comes. He is always here and there at once. One cannot pretend to hide from him. One cannot leave his presence. He is present even where he does not manifest himself.

God has all wisdom. No skill of any creature can dodge him. He is never surprised by anything. He has the solution to everything that may present itself as riddles, challenges, problems or dilemmas.

God is invisible. He cannot be seen in any way. Even in the spiritual world, God cannot be seen. His glory shines too brightly for any creature to contemplate him. So that we may see him, he chooses to reveal himself through Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ is God, he was before coming to earth, he was on earth and he still is today. If you want to see God, look at Jesus Christ.

God is faithful to himself. He lets nothing and no one control him. His plans do not change because of what someone does. He remains equal to himself. God does not react, he acts. He is the one in control of everything. Our prayers, worship or even sins do not move God at all. He is unshakable. He is the everlasting rock (Isa 26:4). God wants us to worship him. But that does not make him more God than he already is. And if we do not worship him, it changes nothing about what he is. God appreciates the moment of our worship because of the contact it creates between him and us so that he can share with us his love and his nature. It is out of love that God asks for our worship. It is out of love that he asks us to love him. It is out of love that he asks us to pray. God is love. He is so full of love that he overflows. If we do not love him, if we do not worship him, if we do not pray, it changes nothing in God. He is self-sufficient. His sovereignty, his omnipotence, his omniscience, his omnipresence, his infinite wisdom, his faithfulness, his justice, his holiness, all of this serves above all God himself. So he needs nothing.

God can therefore do without everything and everyone. But he will not, because it is in his nature to surround himself. He is love. If God found himself obliged to destroy the whole world, he would start creating again. But God will never choose to destroy because that is entirely opposed to his nature. God will always continue to create and recreate in order to finally have a perfect creation. God is good.

The sovereignty of God in the spiritual world

The strength and sovereignty of God, and many other attributes of his person, are well known in the spiritual world. All the angels, the demons and even the devil know that they cannot dare to confront God. Before God, they all tremble (James 2:19).

In the spiritual world, God is the one who makes law. His word is exalted above everything (Psalm 138:2). The angels obey the Word of God (Psalm 103:20). Demons, who are rebellious angels, cannot afford to openly transgress the Word of God. The Word of God is what comes out of his mouth. Jesus Christ is the Word of God who took form in human nature. The Bible is the Word of God embodied in the human system of expression and writing. When we read the Bible in submission to God, we come into contact with Jesus Christ by the Holy Spirit, and we hear God speak. This is called rhema. It is the revealed Word of God. If we believe the Word of God, if we declare it and put it into practice, we control the spiritual world. It is a limit that even the devil will never dare to violate.

The heavens and the earth

The spiritual world includes all invisible space. That therefore includes our immediate environment. But we must understand that God created this space in several dimensions called the heavens and the earth (Genesis 1:1). The heavens are Yahweh’s heavens (Psalm 115:16). The earth is this globe that we inhabit with all its riches. God delegated all this to men. The heavens are directly under the control of God himself. There are three heavens:

  • The aerial heaven or the expanse includes the atmosphere and the clouds; the sky above us, until we reach the stars (Genesis 1:6-8).
  • The starry heaven, in which the sun, the moon and the stars are located (Genesis 1:17).
  • The heaven beyond the stars. This heaven is the residence of God, the angels and the holy spirits (2 Chronicles 2:6). It is into this higher heaven, the dwelling of God, that Paul was taken (2 Corinthians 12:1, etc.).

The spiritual world goes down under the earth and into the seas, for all these places are places where spirits can move. The spiritual world is therefore all around us. And God controls it. It is God who created it and he masters it. Note that when we say God, we speak of the Godhead in its fullness and complexity: the Father, the Son (Jesus Christ), and the Holy Spirit. We do not dare try to describe this divine intimacy. The radiance of glory that escapes from it prevents us from seeing clearly. And if God graciously grants us the revelation of this infinity, we will explode. It is out of love that God remains invisible. Let us stay within the limit God has set for us in order to live fully.

The human being is three-dimensional. He is a spirit who has a soul and lives in a body (1 Thessalonians 5:23). Being a spirit, every human being is thus already connected to the spiritual world. But he may not realize it. Society has so accustomed us since early childhood to what can be seen and what we think that we have the impression that everything stops there. That is how we ignore our spirit in our everyday lives. But whether we ignore it or pay attention to it, the spirit is there and conditions our lives. We can progress by developing our physique and psyche, but a small reversal of the spirit can upset everything. On the other hand, the neglected human spirit is in the pay of the devil and his demons, who will spare no effort to control it and send it adrift. The human spirit is at the mercy of the devil because of sin, which has taken possession of the whole human person (spirit, soul and body).

The new birth

When we come to Christ, our spirit goes through a total regeneration (1 Peter 1:3, 23). This is the new birth (John 3:3). That which is born of the Spirit is spirit. Once this regeneration is done, the Holy Spirit settles in man and unites with his spirit (1 Corinthians 6:17-20).

It is therefore clear in the Word of God, for us who believe in Jesus Christ, that our spirit is already well connected. We are connected to the spiritual world, but more than that we are connected to the right source and this connection cannot be cut. Unless the Holy Spirit himself decides to leave us, no one can dislodge him from us, not even ourselves. The love that holds us is stronger than we are and it has no intention of leaving us. Nothing will be able to separate us from the love of Christ.

Maintaining the connection

We must maintain this connection. It is not to prevent its being cut, which is not possible. It is to live the connection permanently. Indeed, although the connection cannot be cut, it can be suspended. We must take things from the spiritual world to control our physical life and we must also, through our physical life, send signals to control our spiritual environment. The interference of our psyche (soul) and the passions of our body can scramble the signal and cause a suspension in our victorious life. So the connection cannot be cut but our enjoyment of the connection can be suspended. This is what must be prevented by maintaining this connection of our spirit with the Holy Spirit.

To maintain the connection, attention must be given to the Holy Spirit. We must focus on him. We must avoid quenching the Holy Spirit (1 Thessalonians 5:19). That consists in saying no to him. He is very sensitive. If we say NO to him, he will leave us and wait for the right moment to call us back to order. And most of the time, during this interval, we suffer great harm.

Attitudes to adopt

As a Christian, you must also avoid ridiculing the movements of the Spirit either in yourself or in others. This is called blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (Mark 3:28-30). Do not despise prophecies, do not make speaking in tongues a subject of unhealthy jokes, do not mock those who speak in tongues, prophesy or fall into a trance. If you do not have the insight to understand what is going on, turn to the Lord in prayer. You can say to him for example: “Lord, glorify yourself and do not let the enemy find a place here.” And trust God to answer you. Show love for Christians, even if they live spiritual dimensions that you do not understand. And always ask God to give you the grace, if it is truly he who is at work, to live these same dimensions. Desire spiritual gifts. Do not forbid God to act today as in the time of the apostles. In any case, you cannot forbid him anything. Your theory against miracles will only be an obstacle to yourself. Do not quench the Spirit (1 Thessalonians 5:19).

Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. (Eph 4:30) Do not be stubborn in evil. Be sensitive. Repent as soon as you know that you have done wrong. Do not live your own righteousness. If your conscience accuses you, go to God. Examine yourself before his face. If the Holy Spirit convicts you of something, correct yourself following his instructions. But if after examining your conscience there is nothing evident about this accusation, resist the devil. Tell him that you are justified in Christ. Never again ask God’s forgiveness for a sin you have already confessed before. Tell your conscience that you know the blood of Jesus Christ has already washed you from that.

Be careful with anger. Never keep it too long. for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God. (James 1:20) The Holy Spirit is God.

Recommended spiritual practices

Worship God. Spend time saying and singing his attributes, his works and his person. Tell him often that you love him.

Listen to Christian music of worship and praise. This maintains your spirit and opens your soul to the joy of the Holy Spirit.

Read your Bible. Very often. When you read the Bible in submission to God, the Holy Spirit communicates more intensely with your spirit; your soul gains an ever deeper understanding of the mysteries of God and your physical senses find themselves better and better subjected to the will of God. Have an ear only for what gives you faith in God. Prefer messages that glorify God, speak of his goodness, bring you closer to him and to his love.

Listen to the news only to keep yourself informed from time to time. Choose carefully what you are going to listen to or read. Be more focused on God than on the news. You will thus be able to control even the news by acting according to Heaven’s instructions regarding what is happening. We Christians should decide what the head of state will do instead of learning it in the press.

Practice fasting and prayer. Fasting weakens the flesh in its wild desires so that your spirit can be more master of your being. Make time to pray and pray longer. The more time you spend before God, the more you are filled with his person. Stay connected!

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord. Whatever you do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father, through him. (Col 3:16-17)

lecons.titre: The devil dominates the whole world
lecons.html:
This is a title that can puff up his chest, for the devil is a very proud spirit. His pride is his disgrace but he cannot do without it. It is his sickness that will destroy him. God does not need to strike the devil. God does not need to throw him into hell. He will certainly sink into it himself. His pride and his hateful nature already constitute a hell in which he lives. Whoever has hatred can only be unhappy and that is what the devil is.

However, this title is true in a certain way. We know that we are of God, and that the whole world lies in the power of the evil one (1 John 5:19). The devil is the prince of this world (John 12:31), the god of this age (2 Corinthians 4:4), and the whole world is under his power.

The limited reach of Satan’s power

Satan exercises his dominion over the affairs of this world from rulers down to simple individuals. But this is reduced only to the number of people who are unbelievers and refuse to approach God through Jesus Christ. The devil controls only the sons of rebellion. Those who are born of God, by the action of the Holy Spirit, are kept by Jesus Christ the begotten Son of God and the evil one does not touch them (1 John 5:18). The devil is not sovereign of the world. He is nothing other than the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now works in the sons of rebellion (Ephesians 2:2).

The devil therefore has no binding power over the whole world. He exercises his power of domination and control by using the ignorance and allegiance of those who inhabit planet earth. Whoever understands and accepts the Gospel of Jesus Christ frees himself from the influence of the devil. And if, in addition, the person who believed in Jesus Christ progresses in meditation on the Word of God, his knowledge of the truth will progress and the devil will lose more and more ground before this Christian. That is why the devil uses all the artifices of the physical world and of intellectualism to keep people from seeing the splendor of the Gospel shine (2 Corinthians 4:4).

The nature of the devil

The devil is above all a creature of God. He was an angel, a cherub. But afterward, of his own will, without any temptation, he decided to rebel against God. Some of his abilities and strengths remained with him. But God removed him from his position, put him out of the third heaven, which is the dwelling of God. The devil was therefore driven out to the earth. He acts in all dimensions close to the earth. He has agents posted in different places up to the starry heaven. The devil himself does not stay in one place. He goes from place to place in search of worship. Every insult and profanation of the person of God is a joy to him. It is for him an indirect worship of his own person. He is never satisfied and cannot be. He seeks more and more worship and can never have it fully. As soon as he sets up his reign somewhere and begins to receive worship, his nature passes to those who worship him, who in turn begin to want worship. That is why all the followers of worldly and idolatrous religions are full of pride and vain glory. Even their apparent humility is in fact another, more horrible face of their ego. The devil will never entirely have the worship of men as he wants. Apart from the rivalry his own followers give him, the light of the gospel continues to advance and to turn more people away from ungodliness. The devil can therefore only be dissatisfied, unstable, and continually irritated.

The limitations of the devil

The devil is not omniscient. He has a record of the past that he can consult. But he does not know the future. He can predict only by using the course of action and the appetites of the human beings he controls. And besides, he will set rows of demons in motion to bring about his predictions. But he can always fail. The devil does not know what is happening everywhere at the same time. The devil does not know thoughts, especially those of God’s children. The devil can only know what he is made to know in one way or another.

The devil is not omnipotent. He is powerful, very powerful, but his power has limits. The blood of Jesus Christ is one of the impassable limits to the power of the devil. The devil can move mountains, he can create hurricanes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, etc. The devil is quite strong. But if God blows on a stone and sets it on the ground, the devil will not dare touch it because not only will he never be able to lift it, but he risks burning himself.

The devil is so strong that if all the human beings who ever lived on earth got together, they could not resist him. But a simple Christian who has faith in Christ can resist him. The name of Jesus Christ in the mouth of a Christian who has faith is an impassable limit to all the power of the devil. That is why when such a Christian shows up somewhere, the devil and his demons, unable to hide, pack their bags and leave. They do not want to be trampled on.

The devil is not omnipresent. He cannot be everywhere at once. If he is in the United States right now, he cannot at the same time be in Benin. He has a network of demons that informs him but he remains nonetheless limited in space.

The defeat of the devil

The devil’s purposes are always evil. Satan will never do good to anyone. His only aim is to steal, kill and destroy (John 10:10). All the power the devil uses is already broken by the cross of Jesus Christ (Colossians 2:14-15). That is why even though he has the strength to move mountains, he cannot dare touch a little child who believes in Christ. Jesus Christ is the Son of God. He came to destroy the works of the evil one. We are Christ’s ambassadors. We destroy the works of the devil. And nothing will ever be able to harm us (Luke 10:19).

Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you. (Luke 10:19) These are the words of the Almighty. “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!” the disciples could say. Jesus Christ himself confirms that the spirits have been subjected to us.

Demons are fallen angels, the whole angelic company that followed Satan’s revolt. Jesus Christ says they are subject to us. Demons are under Satan’s orders. They are afraid of God. They hate every environment that attracts the glory of God. They cannot live in his company. If you live in an atmosphere of praise and worship, you force the demons to flee.

Classification of demons

The classification of demons that the Bible shows us is simple and clear: rulers, authorities, world rulers of this darkness, spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places. The Bible gives us no other details because we do not need them. All these spirits are subject to us. We do not need to be afraid of their rank or of anything related to them. Although the Lord Jesus tells us that some of these demons come out only by prayer and fasting (and that we must indeed take the exercise of fasting seriously), we are victorious over the whole demonic horde by the same principle: faith in Jesus Christ. With it we are guaranteed the direction of the Holy Spirit and we remain victorious. For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith. Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? (1 John 5:4-5)

What attracts demons

It is not good to let demons take place in your environment. They will infect it by their actions and give you desires you would not normally like. They will try to whisper bad ideas to you to confuse your good ideas. Demons are attracted by everything that has served for false worship such as idols, profane and fetish music, magic movies, objects of idolatry, the literature of sects, etc.

Demons are manipulable to a certain level. Mystical compositions and words can set them in motion. They are looking for worship in order to be like God. So when certain things are done, they use them as an altar to be honored and worshiped. Magic, enchantments, spells, are all ways of devoting oneself to and worshiping demons. Even if the person who gives himself to these practices does not suppose that he is worshiping the spirits he invokes, even if he does no veneration or prostration, the demons consider him their worshiper. This is a principle of the spiritual world. Every person worships what he invokes for a favor. Prayer itself is a form of worship. That is why God forbids practices that lead to the invocation of spirits. The following Bible texts are not suggestions. They are mandatory for anyone who wants to be of God:

“You shall not allow a sorceress to live. (Exod 22:18)

There shall not be found with you anyone who makes his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, one who uses divination, one who tells fortunes, or an enchanter, or a sorcerer, or a charmer, or someone who consults with a familiar spirit, or a wizard, or a necromancer. For whoever does these things is an abomination to Yahweh. Because of these abominations, Yahweh your God drives them out from before you. You shall be blameless with Yahweh your God. (Deut 18:10-13)

“ ‘A man or a woman that is a medium or is a wizard shall surely be put to death. They shall be stoned with stones. Their blood shall be upon themselves.’ ” (Lev 20:27)

When they tell you, “Consult with those who have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter,” shouldn’t a people consult with their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living? Turn to the law and to the covenant! If they don’t speak according to this word, surely there is no morning for them. (Isa 8:19-20)

Demons are also attracted by everything related to sexual immorality, lust, orgies. They love atmospheres of hatred, quarreling and war. The more one gives oneself to these things, the more one attracts demons who reinforce one’s bad actions and make people slaves of their vices.

Demonic strongholds

Certain families and places have thus become arenas of certain vices. The first occupants, having begun to live in a certain way, attracted demons who turned this place into their stronghold. This is also the case with certain living conditions such as poverty, idleness, unemployment, etc. It is enough for an individual to come to live in this place for his story to become quite different. He will begin to be strongly tempted to live these vices. His living condition will also find itself obliged to match those who live in the environment.

Even God’s children are not safe from this danger. They must be watchful and pray to overcome. Moreover, they must overcome and definitively overthrow the stronghold; otherwise, with a little carelessness, they can find themselves entirely on the ground. Places, families, nations can at any moment become such strongholds and these strongholds must be overthrown.

It should be noted that when the apostle Paul speaks of strongholds and describes them as reasonings, he says exactly the same thing as what precedes. Indeed, the reasonings that the apostle calls strongholds are the heights that rise up against the knowledge of Christ (2 Corinthians 10:4-5). Now it is the prince of this world who keeps people from seeing the splendor of the Gospel, in other words from knowing Christ (2 Corinthians 4:4). Which means that the reasoning-strongholds the apostle Paul speaks of are in reality the heights fortified by the devil and his agents. The weapons of our warfare are not fleshly. It is not only a matter of reasonings opposed to reasonings. These are offensive and defensive weapons of righteousness. We fight more in prayer and at this level no one actually reasons.

Individuals have grazed for a long time on thoughts that opened the door to demons who have long inhabited their souls, strengthening them in these bad thoughts and giving them lifestyles that are against godliness. If they are not delivered, they will pass these bad lifestyles on to many others by contact, by friendship and by descent. With each evolution, the grip of this evil will be strengthened and extended. It must be stopped.

How to defeat demons

To defeat them, you must begin by praying. With prayer, the demons will go away. Then the word of God will find a place in the hearts of these people to renew the mind and close the door to evil spirits. In any case, it is recommended that a Christian inform himself about his environment and the places where he will live. He must also watch and pray so as not to let demonic influences give him a lifestyle that ridicules his faith in Christ.

When you arrive somewhere, begin by getting rid of everything related to idolatry, magic, sects, sexual immorality as far as it is in your power. The literature of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Mormons, the Moon sect and Branham’s books are also objects of demonic attraction that must be got rid of. Avoid listening to and singing worldly music. It carries words that give access to demons.

Pray and sanctify the place. Praise and worship God aloud. Invoke the name of Jesus Christ and the blood of Jesus Christ. The light will flood the place and the demons will flee with all their baggage.

Demonic altars

Other things that support the activity of demons are altars. They are necessarily erected by men intentionally. The aim of the one who erects an altar is often to obtain a favor from a spirit. These altars are visible just about everywhere in places dominated by idolatry. These are the fetishes and convents that are seen just about everywhere. As soon as objects are arranged in a precise way and incantations are made, spirits come to lodge there and these things and places become altars. Sometimes it is the spirits themselves who choose their places. They often manifest there to the knowledge of the followers of occultism to lead them to erect altars in the place. A place remains an altar even when physically the things have been moved and no more worship is done in the place. Every object or place that has served for worship continues for the spirit to be its altar. It will stay there and try to harm anyone who comes into contact with this place or object. But if it finds an opening in this person, it leads him to reestablish its worship.

When a Christian finds himself in a place that is an altar, or in the environment of an altar, his spirit will show a certain discomfort (Acts 17:16). He must take up the offensive weapons of righteousness and engage in the fight by prayer and then by evangelization as soon as openings occur. Altars are the foundations of strongholds. Every environment that is a stronghold of a certain baseness of life is under the control of an altar. The altar sees to subjecting every person to the domination of the spirits controlling the environment. If it sees resistance in the person, it will try to break it by using seductions. If that does not work, the altar will provoke uprisings to destroy the Christian or send him away from the place. Altars are great fortifications because the demons that work there are not those small wandering demons. They are giants who want to be worshiped as gods. There are other altars that have been established solely for the purpose of harming another person. Places that are neglected altars are often poles of great dramas.

Every altar must be addressed and destroyed. Jesus Christ the Son of God came to destroy the works of the evil one and we are Christ’s ambassadors. We must take hold of the Word of God to dethrone these spirits that want worship. You will speak to them thus: “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’ ” (Jer 10:11) When you speak to an altar, the demon that lodges there hears and bends the knee. If you drive it out, it will go away. Which means that the altar is destroyed.

Yahweh has established his throne in the heavens. His kingdom rules over all. Praise Yahweh, you angels of his, who are mighty in strength, who fulfill his word, obeying the voice of his word. Praise Yahweh, all you armies of his, you servants of his, who do his pleasure. (Ps 103:19-21)

Besides the multitude of angels who lost their dignities by following Satan’s side, a more impressive number still exists in God’s service. In biblical terms, their number is “ten thousands of ten thousands, and thousands of thousands” (Rev 5:11; Dan 7:10; Ps 68:17). If we analyze these verses, the number of angels is simply undefinable. They are innumerable. Their ranks and classifications are as impressive as their number.

Angelic ranks

The archangels

Archangels are the principal chiefs of the angels. The Bible particularly mentions only one, who is Michael (Daniel 10:13-21; Daniel 12:1; Jude 1:9; Revelation 12:7). The second angel expressly named in the Bible is Gabriel (Daniel 8:16; Daniel 9:21; Luke 1:19-26; Matthew 1:20; Matthew 2:13-19). It is not expressly said in the Bible that Gabriel is an archangel. It is commentaries that designate him as such because of the roles he played in the Bible. The voice of an archangel will immediately precede the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ (1 Thessalonians 4:16). If it is neither Michael nor Gabriel, then the number of archangels is more than two.

The Cherubim

God sits enthroned on the Cherubim (Genesis 3:24; Exodus 25:18-20; Psalm 18:10; Ezekiel 1:4-28; Ezekiel 8:1-4; Ezekiel 10:1-22). From what is written, we see the cherubim in the roles of carrying God’s throne, serving as his chariot and guarding the way of access to God’s glory. They will kill anyone who ventures closer to God than he allows. And to protect everything that has the value of God’s nature against all corruption, the Cherubim are the angels who intervene (Genesis 3:24). Satan before his fall was a cherub, perhaps their chief (Isaiah 14:12; Ezekiel 28:14). But not having kept his dignity, he became viler than a serpent and wants to be seen as a dragon to impress. It is false noise. It is the Cherubim in God’s service who make a magnificent noise with their wings, proof of their dignity (Ezekiel 1:24-25).

The Seraphim

The seraphim are mentioned only once in the Bible (Isaiah 6:1-7). Called the Burning Ones (like fire), they are among the angels closest to God’s throne and sing his glory and holiness. They are more graceful than the Cherubim. To atone for the sin of the repentant Isaiah, a seraph came with a burning coal from the altar. By contrast, the burning coal from between the wheels of the cherubim will destroy rebellious cities (Ezekiel 10:2).

The four living creatures

The four living creatures (Revelation 4:6-9; 5:8) are closer to God than the Cherubim and seraphim because they are directly inside and all around God’s throne. They sing God’s glory continually. They may also be cherubim like the four living creatures Ezekiel saw and described. But these seem to be of a higher rank. They are in the throne. They have certain traits of the cherubim described by Ezekiel, but also of the Seraphim described by Isaiah, and they are less hybrid. They had eyes all around (they are covered with eyes), they see everything and have the ability to be both in the midst of and around the throne. A certain dimension of omnipresence and omniscience. No wonder lightnings, voices and thunders come out of the throne. They have the secret of the most hidden things of God. They are able to know the meaning of the seals that the lamb breaks (Revelation 6:1-7).

The watchers

The watchers are those who keep watch (Daniel 4:13, 17, 23). They are angels jealous for the glory of God, who see to it that it manifests on earth and that no one steals it. It was a watcher who ordered the judgment of partial madness on Nebuchadnezzar for glorifying himself with the glory of God. It was probably one of them who struck Herod for not giving glory to God (Acts 12:20-24).

The seven thunders

The seven thunders are not directly described in Revelation. Even their number may be figurative, seven being fullness (Revelation 10:3-4). The first time we hear a voice of thunder in the New Testament is when the Father answers the Son saying that he has already glorified his name and would do so again (John 12:28-29). In John’s Revelation, we see God’s majestic movements accompanied by voices and thunders. The thunders are therefore the witnesses of the extraordinary power of the Word of God. They are the voice of God and manifest his authority as creator, therefore owner of everything and having every right to do what he wants.

The psalmist had a revelation of it: Yahweh’s voice is on the waters. The God of glory thunders, even Yahweh on many waters. Yahweh’s voice is powerful. Yahweh’s voice is full of majesty. Yahweh’s voice breaks the cedars. Yes, Yahweh breaks in pieces the cedars of Lebanon. He makes them also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young, wild ox. Yahweh’s voice strikes with flashes of lightning. Yahweh’s voice shakes the wilderness. Yahweh shakes the wilderness of Kadesh. Yahweh’s voice makes the deer calve, and strips the forests bare. In his temple everything says, “Glory!” (Ps 29:3-9)

When the thunders intervene, judgment is imminent, not to say immediate, and moreover irreversible. They are God’s heavy and irresistible weapons (Psalm 18:13-14).

The angelic organization

Angels are organized into Principalities, powers, thrones, authorities, dominions (Ephesians 1:21; Ephesians 3:10; Colossians 1:16; Colossians 2:10; 1 Peter 3:22). We cannot say which comes first. When we try to contemplate them together, we perceive an army, a structure and an organization more impressive than human imagination can ever embrace. It is more than magnificent.

Everything we have cited and lightly (not to say clumsily) described is only the revealed part of God’s army. It is like the visible part of the iceberg. The greater part is outside our field of vision. If all these angelic beings with so much power are only creatures of God that he made just with his Word, can you imagine the greatness and power of God himself? God in himself has all the power of the angelic creatures gathered together in infinitely multiplied intensity. Hearing the voice of a thunder is terrible. Hearing the voice of God is hearing the voice of an infinite multitude of thunders. Looking at the sun is terrible for the eyes. Looking at an angel in the radiance of his glory is even more terrible. Looking at God is like looking at a light with the intensity of the sun multiplied by a trillion times a trillion times infinity.

Do you believe you could survive looking at him? Do you realize the reason why God does not want to let us see him in his full dimension? And do you see how great his love is that he chose to find a way to reveal himself through the incarnation of his only Son Jesus Christ, our Lord? Let us show gratitude for this love, by giving glory to God through Jesus Christ. He is the image of the invisible God. In him dwells bodily all the fullness of the Godhead.

The ministry of angels

All the angels in their various ranks and glory are in God’s service, carrying out his orders and working in his army. They can take the form of fire and winds in the exercise of their ministry (Hebrews 1:7). Among their number is a great multitude working directly for the care of God’s children in Jesus Christ (Hebrews 1:14). If we must speak of guardian angels, it would be these.

So one cannot say that an unbeliever has a guardian angel, even if it is a baby. If his parents are not believers who surround him with prayer, no angel would watch over him permanently. God in his sovereignty can bring angels to intervene on behalf of an unbeliever for a specific reason and for the purpose of a plan of redemption (Acts 10:1-6). When people say that they can speak to their guardian angels at special times and by certain alchemies, they must be made to understand that they are communicating only with demons posing as angels of light. Without Christ, you have no angels in your care. And even in Christ, you cannot start a conversation with an angel. It will always be the other way around and in line with the Word of God.

Every person who believes in Jesus Christ has a troop of angels who take care of him directly. These angels constantly have access to the presence of God in heaven, probably because of the faith of their charge in Jesus Christ (Matthew 18:10). Angels apply themselves to our safety and other needs that fall within their job description. They are involved in our everyday life and accompany us in ministry (Psalm 34:7; Psalm 91:11-12; Acts 5:17-20; Acts 8:26; Revelation 19:10; 22:8-9).

Our relationship with angels

Angels work for us and with us. But angels are not under our orders. We cannot just command them, send them off to do this and that just as we please. Angels are in God’s service. They obey only his voice. No prayer or way of doing things can compel an angel into action. He will always wait to receive his orders before acting. It is possible for angels to go into action immediately when we pray. But that does not mean we commanded it. It means that our prayer activated a directive of the Word of God that falls within that angel’s job description. He therefore acts in obedience to the Word of God, that is, to the voice of God.

Angels are attracted only by the presence of God. The atmosphere they prefer is praise and worship of God. They also like the company of God’s children who live in sanctification and are in God’s service. Angels do not live in environments of sin. They keep away from the works of the flesh. If your attitude, thoughts, words and actions glorify God, you will always be surrounded by angels. The more your spiritual atmosphere glorifies God, the more angels will be with you and the more they will act in your interest.

Angels do not steal God’s worship. Any angel who receives worship is not truly an angel. It is a demon in search of worship that has transformed itself into an angel of light to deceive its victims as their chief, the devil, also does. These are those so-called angels that are invoked with perfumes, incense or mystical compositions and esoteric words. They are not angels, they are demons. Every child of God must keep away from all worship of angels.

True angels do not steal God’s worship (Revelation 22:8-9). They worship God, they want all worship to turn to God. When angels sense worship directed to them, either they correct you or they move away from you. Generally it is the latter. For angels can communicate with humans only under direct order from God. No angel will appear and speak with a man on his own initiative. It will necessarily be to bring a message from God. And the message an angel brings will never depart from the holiness of the Word of God, the Bible.

Activating the ministry of angels

Activating the ministry of angels is not something you say. It is something done by putting the Word of God into practice, prayer in the will of God, reading the Bible, evangelism, worship and praise directed to God. Avoid saying things like this: “I command the angels…, I activate the ministry of angels…, I want the angels to go…” These words risk driving them away.

Angels will not worship you. They will not obey you. They worship God, they are in his service and they obey him alone. A supposed angel who does not stay within this framework is in fact a demon in disguise. Drive him out in the name of Jesus Christ.

As the police in the service of the state work for the good of the population, the angels in God’s service work for the good of God’s children.

In the spiritual world, Jesus Christ is at the top rank of the hierarchy. He is the head of every dominion and authority. He is before all and everyone. He is above everything. He is the King, the supreme sovereign. He is God. In the spiritual world, there is only one throne where God sits despite his complexity (Father, Son and Holy Spirit). The whole revelation of God is Jesus Christ. God dwells in unapproachable light. That is to say, he cannot be seen by any creature unless he manifests himself and takes a form that allows spiritual or physical creatures to see him. Jesus Christ is the whole revelation of God. He is the image of the invisible God. Even in the spiritual world, God is invisible. His manifestation is Jesus Christ. You will never see the Father and you will never see the Holy Spirit. In the physical or in the spiritual, you will see only Jesus Christ alone.

The biblical revelation

This is clearly demonstrated in the Bible.

He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.” (Exod 33:20)

All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows the Son, except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son desires to reveal him. (Matt 11:27)

Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God. He has seen the Father. (John 6:46)

He alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen, nor can see: to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen. (1 Tim 6:16)

No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us. (1 John 4:12)

Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you such a long time, and do you not know me, Philip? He who has seen me has seen the Father. How do you say, ‘Show us the Father?’ Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? The words that I tell you, I speak not from myself; but the Father who lives in me does his works. Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me; or else believe me for the very works’ sake. (John 14:8-11)

I and the Father are one.” (John 10:30)

The two dimensions of the authority of Jesus Christ

That is why the name of Jesus Christ is the most feared in the spiritual world. Because the Sovereign is he. The authority of Jesus Christ is in two dimensions:

First, he is God. Which means he has power over everything. So he does not need to be given power. He has authority over all things. He does not need a delegated authority. He can make the decision to do what he wants. He does not need to follow the will of another. Everything was created by him and for him, so that if things do not go according to his plans, he can get rid of what he wants and do what he wants. But Jesus Christ did not use this authority. When he was on earth, he did not use it at all. Up to today, he does not in fact use it. It is only in unity with the other persons of the Godhead that he makes use of this authority. If he makes use of this authority and takes an action, we will not say that Jesus Christ did such a thing, we will rather say that God did it. And when we say that God did such a thing, we will not be able to specify which person of the Divine Trinity acted. This is what the apostle Paul is speaking of when he says that at a given moment the Lord Jesus Christ (the Son) will hand over authority to him who is God and Father so that God may be all in all (1 Corinthians 15:27-28). This does not mean that the Lord Jesus would come down from the throne. And it does not mean that another throne will be placed above him. There is only one throne in heaven on which God sits. And there is only one God. The same who manifested himself in the person of Jesus Christ our Lord. And God wanted all the fullness of the Godhead to dwell bodily in Jesus Christ (Colossians 2:9).

The second dimension of the authority of Jesus Christ is the one he acquired through his saving work. Indeed, by accepting to be the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, and by taking upon himself all our sins, in obedience to the Father, he defeated in every sense and everywhere, all enemies. By this victory, he took back the authority that Adam had handed over by disobedience into the hands of the devil. This is in fact the reason why on earth, our Lord made use of his authority only in the dimension of the Son of God and even more of the Son of Man. Because he is the second Adam. He came to fight the fight that the offspring of the woman must fight for the restoration of fallen humanity in the glory of God. And he fought it by living a life of obedience to the will of God as it is expressed in the Scriptures, as every man should. He is the only one to succeed in this and to take our dominion back from the hands of the devil. It is of this authority that our Lord Jesus Christ spoke when, after his resurrection, he presented himself to the disciples and said: “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” (Matthew 28:18)

The authority delegated to believers

This authority, the Lord gave back to us through his name: He said to them, “Go into all the world, and preach the Good News to the whole creation. He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who disbelieves will be condemned. These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages; they will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will in no way hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.” (Mark 16:15-18)

This truth is even more exposed in Paul’s letter to the Philippians: Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus, who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross. Therefore God also highly exalted him, and gave to him the name which is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth, and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. (Phil 2:5-11)

The power of the name of Jesus Christ

When the name of Jesus Christ is pronounced, the whole spiritual world pays attention. As soon as the use of his name truly involves the person of the Lord Jesus Christ, the whole spiritual world yields. In other words, when a child of God invokes the name of Jesus Christ by faith and in line with the Word of God, his word is law in the spiritual world. Everything he says will be done and the manifestation in the physical world will come very quickly. When the name of Jesus Christ is invoked with faith, the presence of the Lord manifests with his irresistible, blinding, terrifying and unapproachable light.

Angels pay attention when they hear the name of Jesus Christ pronounced. He is their supreme Chief, above the highest of the archangels. When they hear words spoken in the name of Jesus Christ in line with the will of God, they go into action, if these words fall within their job description. They may ask for instructions to confirm that they must act, but they cannot remain indifferent when the name of Jesus Christ is invoked.

Demons pay attention to the name of Jesus Christ. They are subject to his power, even if they do not want to be under his direction. When the name of Jesus Christ is pronounced, they therefore take care not to find themselves dazzled by his presence. If the name of Jesus Christ is invoked with faith by a child of God, the demons panic and tumble. Indeed, they are immediately dazzled by the presence of God, tremble and flee. It is not possible for demons to resist before the presence of Jesus Christ in a Christian’s life. Unless the latter lets them dwell. But if the Christian commands the demon to leave, they will run.

Nothing resists the name of Jesus Christ in the mouth of a child of God who puts his trust in the Word of God.

lecons.titre: The blood of Jesus Christ, the infallible weapon
lecons.html:
Have you heard of the war that took place in Heaven? The objective was to expel the rebel and his troop. The archangel Michael and his angels lined up for battle against the dragon and his demons. The fight was serious and rough but the dragon and his troop were defeated and thrown out of God’s Heaven. This victory was made possible by the intervention of an irresistible weapon: the blood of the Lamb (Revelation 12:7-11).

Before the blood of Jesus Christ, the devil loses all power. One of the strong weapons the devil uses is accusation. And that does not hold before the blood of Jesus Christ, which cleanses us from all sin (1 John 1:7). The cleansing that the blood of Jesus Christ does for us is constant and eternal because it is the blood of an eternal covenant (Hebrews 13:20).

The cry of the blood of Jesus Christ

The blood of Jesus Christ speaks better than the blood of Abel (Hebrews 12:24). The blood of the innocent Abel cries from the earth to Heaven perhaps demanding justice or rather vengeance, that is, the punishment of the murderer. The blood of Jesus Christ cries louder. The voice of the blood of Jesus Christ asks nothing for Jesus Christ himself. Jesus Christ is God and all-sufficient. He needs nothing. The voice of the blood of Jesus Christ pleads justice for us: “I have already paid the price, they are free and deserve the glory of God. Release them and compensate them for all the time they were in servitude. For I have paid everything from beginning to end.”

If we consider the whole message of the Word of God the Bible, the cry of the blood of Jesus Christ can be interpreted or summarized like this. But since it is to God that it speaks, it is fitting to leave to God the decoding of this code. The altar (Revelation 9:13; Exodus 30:10) and the blood of the Lamb understand each other and God understands them. The good news is that it speaks well of us because it is the blood of Jesus Christ poured out for us (Luke 22:20).

The use of the blood of Jesus Christ

In prayer, we can cover ourselves with the blood of Jesus Christ, use it to purify our spiritual environment, use it to mark with a seal forbidding the enemy everything that belongs to us and thus always remain victorious. Indeed, the presence of the blood of Jesus Christ drives away all demons and strengthens the angels. The blood of Jesus Christ has multiple spiritual virtues. We can use it as needed by following the direction of the Holy Spirit. The blood of Jesus Christ is the weapon that annihilates the devil.

The Holy Spirit is one of the three persons of the Godhead. Although he is a whole person in himself, he makes himself the property of the other persons of the Godhead and remains discreet. He is the Spirit of God and the Spirit of Jesus Christ. He refuses to take a form. He loves spirit, that is, breath. The other forms he can take in his manifestation are water and oil. The river of the water of life, clear as crystal, which flows from the throne of God and of the lamb (Revelation 22:1), whose channels gladden the City of God (Psalm 46:5), the precious oil that, poured on the head, runs down on the beard and the edges of Aaron’s garments (Psalm 133:2) are nothing other than the Holy Spirit. He also loves the form of cloud, smoke and light that surpasses the brightness of the sun.

The nature of the Holy Spirit

The Holy Spirit is the presence of God. No manifestation of the Godhead can happen without the Holy Spirit introducing it by a sound of a rushing wind, a blinding light, fire or water clear as crystal. The Holy Spirit is the power from on high (Luke 24:49; Acts 1:4-5). That is why his full manifestation is always accompanied by supernatural movements. Even when the Holy Spirit whispers, the one who hears him trembles with his whole being. The Holy Spirit has this versatility because he is by himself the seven eyes of the lamb, the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth (Revelation 5:6).

In his dealings with us humans, the Holy Spirit never takes a form to present himself personally. He takes the forms of the Lord Jesus Christ. The Holy Spirit makes himself the comforter like the Lord Jesus Christ or advocate, intercessor, teacher, director, guide, etc. The Holy Spirit does everything in the name of Jesus Christ. He takes what is Christ’s and gives it to us. It is the Holy Spirit who identifies us with the atoning work of Jesus Christ, applying his death and resurrection to us, who communicates to us the gifts of God’s grace, who operates the gifts in us and who leads us in ministry. Everything that is the prerogative of the Father and the Son in us, the Holy Spirit does without being seen. The only things the Holy Spirit does in his own name consist in being on us the mark that identifies us as Christ’s property and in communicating with our spirit to assure us within ourselves that we are children of God (Ephesians 1:13; Romans 8:15; 2 Corinthians 1:22; Ephesians 4:30).

The communication of the Holy Spirit

The communication of the Holy Spirit with our spirit is constant and permanent. Even when in the noise of life’s worries and the desires of the flesh we do not hear him, he continues to communicate with our spirit. That is why as soon as we withdraw to seek the face of God, it generally does not take us long to start receiving instructions and directives. He may begin by leading us into repentance, worship, meditation and go deeper and deeper.

To receive anything from God, we must go through communication with the Holy Spirit. You can speak to him now and he will answer you. He will never refuse to answer. The Holy Spirit’s answers may not immediately be what we expect but he will answer, bring us back on track if need be, and clear up the questions of our heart.

The works of the Holy Spirit

The first thing the Holy Spirit does in a human life is the conviction of sin. As soon as the person is exposed to the Gospel, the Holy Spirit convinces him of his state as a sinner and a hopelessly lost soul. Then he gives him the conviction that Jesus Christ is the Savior and calls him to accept this gift. As soon as the person accepts Jesus Christ as his Lord and Savior, the Holy Spirit enters him and applies to him the cleansing of the blood of Jesus Christ. The Holy Spirit cleans house in him and regenerates his spirit by the creative effect of the Word of God. Then, he settles in the born-again spirit and becomes one with it (1 Corinthians 6:17).

From then on, the Holy Spirit acts in this new child of God as an inner anointing that teaches and leads him into the truth. He warns him against dangers and signals to him the presence of false teachings or false teachers (1 John 2:20-27). This perception can be very hard to recognize at first. But a person who is truly born again will know the direction of the Holy Spirit from within and will not easily fall prey to wolves.

The baptism in the Holy Spirit

The next action of the Holy Spirit on the child of God is the baptism in the Holy Spirit. The Lord Jesus Christ releases on the Christian a measure of his person and power through the Holy Spirit. It is an investiture of power to be a witness of Jesus Christ in everyday life in thoughts, words and actions. It is a movement by which the Holy Spirit takes possession of the person’s whole being. In addition to his spirit, the Holy Spirit makes himself master of the person’s soul and body. When the Holy Spirit enters this role, he first attacks the organ that is the most uncontrollable in the human body: the tongue (James 3:5-8). The person baptized in the Holy Spirit will speak in other languages and proclaim the wonders of God.

Too many useless arguments circulate against this action of the Holy Spirit. But God does not apologize. If a person, basing himself on the teachings he preferred to believe, refuses to let the Holy Spirit be master of his whole person, the comforter would content himself with his initial role. He forces no one. But it is not possible for the Holy Spirit to have total control of your life as long as from your heart you prevent him from having access to your tongue.

Speaking in tongues

Do not be afraid to speak in tongues. You cannot say just anything. The Holy Spirit takes charge of what must come out. Besides, you can perceive in your spirit (your inner being) what must be said. The fear lies in the fact that what you perceive from within seems to make no sense. And yet it is exactly what must be said. It is your spirit that prays, receiving instruction from the Holy Spirit; accompany it. Repeat what it says and keep going, even if it seems to you to be nonsense. That is how you speak in tongues. The Holy Spirit gives the utterance and you speak.

Obviously, it can begin with words you understand and continue with things you do not understand. It can even alternate. Live the experience fully by trusting God. You are in his hands. It is not possible for a demon to step in. They would not dare enter his Holy Presence. Unclean spirits do not enter places where God is glorified. The glory of God is an environment that a demon will never want to inhabit. So let yourself go into the hands of the Almighty. Pray in the spirit.

We have already said above the things to avoid doing to the Holy Spirit. So it is no longer necessary to return to them here. Always remember that the Holy Spirit is God. He loves you, he will never abandon you, and nothing is outside his control. Say good things to the Holy Spirit very often, especially that you love him and trust him.

lecons.titre: Prayer in tongues, a direct opening
lecons.html:
To pass immediately into the spiritual realm, begin to worship God and to pray in tongues. It is a direct opening. Stop worrying about the controversies on the subject of various kinds of tongues. Just know that if you speak in tongues, you are speaking to God and he understands you. Moreover, in the spirit you say mysteries (1 Corinthians 14:2). You then use the language of men and of angels without the restrictions of your knowledge and intelligence. You tap more strongly into the resources of the Holy Spirit, for it is he who gives your spirit the utterance. You are in a communication that even confuses the demons. You speak with God of secrets that they cannot understand, because only God understands the inexpressible sighs of his Spirit (Romans 8:26-27).

The advantages of prayer in tongues

If prayer consists of conversing with God and him alone, I believe that praying in tongues is the best prayer there is. Because there I can speak to God without worrying about the fact that someone might hear what I say. Besides, it is the only form of prayer that lets my spirit be master in prayer. For if I pray in tongues, my spirit prays (1 Corinthians 14:14). So I will pray by the spirit and I will sing by the spirit regularly, for in this way I build myself up in the will of God and keep myself in his love (1 Corinthians 14:3, 15; Jude 1:20-21).

Prayer in tongues stops the tumultuous waves of the soul to let us hear, see and speak directly in the spiritual realm. This does not mean that the brain shuts down. Quite the opposite, it can function exponentially. But since you are using the resources of the Holy Spirit through your human spirit, you can intervene further than your knowledge allows.

Prayer in tongues puts your soul at rest. It enjoys God’s rest. Even your body is restored. You can experience refreshments and healings in your psychology and your body simply by praying in tongues. All this is part of the building up that the one who speaks in tongues gives himself.

How to receive the gift of tongues

A Christian who does not yet have the grace of praying in tongues must desire it and ask God. Or rather ask to be baptized in the Holy Spirit. Jesus promised that God will give good things to those who ask him (Matthew 7:11). He will receive it immediately if he puts his faith into action and speaks.

As it is clear that there are always people who are slow of understanding and delay acting by faith, we advise every Christian to spend long moments regularly in worshiping God with all his heart. This is not necessary to receive the baptism in the Holy Spirit, but every Christian can also pass immediately into the spiritual world and arrive even directly in God’s palace by worshiping God wholeheartedly. By confessing with your mouth your love for God, appreciating his graces and giving glory to his name for who he is, you enter immediately into the presence of God in his very palace. This revelation is coded in the following verse: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise. Give thanks to him, and bless his name. (Ps 100:4)

If you abound in this direction, if you give yourself moments that you spend before God worshiping him, your spirit will have more and more deep communication with its creator. And it will not be long before you find yourself speaking in tongues.

In the spiritual world, nothing is completely fixed. The base is always floating. It is like a ship on the sea. The only thing that serves as anchor, rudder and foundation is the word. The Word of God is the principal one. Every spirit respects the Word of God. When the Word of God is involved, nothing resists, nothing opposes and nothing moves in the opposite direction. Everything obeys the Word of God. Good and evil spirits all respect the Word of God.

The power of words

But evil spirits, although they respect the Word of God, do not want to submit to it. They know that by following the Word of God in its right sense, they cannot carry out their evil works. For this, they use legalistic places and places of condemnation to subject the ignorant and unbelieving to servitude. So they base their action against their victim on the latter’s ignorance concerning the Word of God and on their negative and evil confessions. In this, the unclean spirits do not violate the Word of God, quite the opposite. For the Bible says: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.” (Matt 12:37) A man’s stomach is filled with the fruit of his mouth. With the harvest of his lips he is satisfied. Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit. (Prov 18:20-21)

Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles. (Prov 21:23) This is not only by avoiding trouble with humans, but by avoiding giving demons a fertile ground from which to make evil sprout against himself.

The danger of the tongue

The tongue is naturally full of deadly venom. And if we leave the tongue unbridled, it will set a deadly fire to all the dimensions of our lives by giving evil spirits the words on which to base themselves to direct all evils toward us (James 3:6, 8). The real problem is that the tongue is uncontrollable by human strength. For every kind of animal, bird, creeping thing, and sea creature, is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind; but nobody can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison. (James 3:7-8) A person not regenerated in Christ will not be able to keep from destroying himself by his own tongue.

The danger of destruction by the tongue also threatens Christians. The enemy powers, having no other possibilities of easy access to the life and possessions of God’s children, watch for the slightest words from their mouths that stray from faith in the Word of God, in order to rush upon them. That is why the apostle exhorts God’s children in these terms: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear. (Eph 4:29) nor filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not appropriate, but rather giving of thanks. (Eph 5:4)

Do not speak until you have something gracious to say about yourself. You must also avoid saying negative things about others. The effect can backfire. Just as the peace you wish upon a house can return to you (Luke 10:5-6), so the evil you declare on others can come back to you. So the Bible urges us never to open our mouths except to bless: Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don’t curse. (Rom 12:14) not rendering evil for evil, or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing. (1 Pet 3:9)

God’s use of our words

God himself uses our words. He needs our words to line up with the truths and promises of his almighty Word in order to activate or deactivate certain laws and principles of the spiritual world. That is why God notes even the least of our conversations in order to use them to our advantage (Malachi 3:16). God keeps the record of our words when we speak with his fear in our heart. God wants us to dare to speak for our justification, for our victory, for our blessing. He wants us to speak by joining our words to his. This sets in motion the creative power of the Word of God.

But as we have already said above, the tongue is uncontrollable by human power or will. Only the power of the Holy Spirit can master it. To avoid stumbling in words, pray a lot in the spirit (in tongues) and give yourself more of the right and duty of silence. Read your Bible a lot and meditate on it so that your mind is renewed and draws its resources from it. And when you must speak, leave your Father’s spirit time to speak through you.

In the spiritual world, grace is not only a concept we define as undeserved favor. Grace is tangible and can take whatever forms it wants to reach its objectives in the life of its target. Grace begins by taking the form of mercy. It thus intervenes to suspend or even remove judgment. It suspends judgment while waiting for the person to accept the divine solution by faith. As soon as this is done, grace removes judgment and restores without fail all privileges and honors (Matthew 9:13; 1 Timothy 1:13-16). Grace always amplifies more and more to slow down judgment, and to manage to remove it as soon as there is repentance (Romans 5:20). Grace has this potential because it is the effect of the atoning work of Jesus Christ. It is the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Grace fights sin

Grace has sin as its enemy. It does not want to let it exist. It fights it in every way. Grace always shows up where sin shows up. Its purpose is to keep sin from causing death as it is accustomed to do, and above all to keep it from taking root and enslaving the attacked person. Grace at first sight presents itself and covers the person. In this way, it delays judgment and positions itself as a teacher to draw the conscience toward repentance (Titus 2:11-12).

Grace must save because it is the source of salvation (Titus 2:11-13). Grace is an instrument of justice in the hands of God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, to guarantee the lives of men and particularly of God’s children. We must ask God, more than often, to show us grace.

The manifestations of grace

Grace also takes the form of competence and aptitude. A person with no training or very little will suddenly acquire a skill and serve in areas where no one would suspect him. This is the work of grace. Grace can make someone particularly excellent in the field of his competences. The Apostle Paul obtained a particular grace that led him to brave terrible situations and announce the Gospel in the whole known world of his time. He wrote more than all the other authors of the Bible and spoke of the mysteries of God extraordinarily. It is not because he was a Pharisee or a Roman or even because he studied under Gamaliel. It is the work of the grace of God in Jesus Christ. The Apostle himself testifies: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God. But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me. (1 Cor 15:9-10) (see also 1 Timothy 1:12-16)

When you ask for grace, you are certain to go further than you have the right and the capacity to. And God loves to show grace and he always will. Grace is the manifestation of God’s goodness (Romans 11:32). Grace meets all needs, even financial and material. And God is able to make all grace abound to you, that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work. (2 Cor 9:8) Always ask God to give you his grace. His presence will guarantee you against useless pains. With grace, you will never lack anything and you do not need to work for everything. Grace is free.

Grace and the Holy Spirit

The Holy Spirit bases all his dealings with us on grace. That is why all the gifts of the Holy Spirit are called charisma, that is, gifts of grace. It is also why the Holy Spirit, although he is the holy God whose eyes cannot behold sin, remains in us despite all our falls into sins of every form. He covers his eyes with grace.

With grace, you will never lack resources. We must take seriously this command of the apostle: You therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. (2 Tim 2:1)

Speaking of our relationship with the spiritual world, we cannot forget the visions and voices whose origins are beyond our senses. Every perception is called vision. So we have a physical vision that relates to what our eyes see physically. When the psyche is considered, personal imaginations of a situation or a future can be called vision. This is entirely supposition accompanied by the desire to be able to accomplish it by paying the price. The strength of one’s desires and their occupying the brain can provoke visions of sleep called dreams (Ecclesiastes 5:3). When a person’s brain experiences disturbances, he may see things that do not exist. At this level, we speak of hallucinations. Spiritual visions are beyond all these things.

Spiritual visions

When, in relation to the spiritual world, we speak of vision, it is the ability to see into the spiritual world in a full or allegorical way. You can then see angels, demons, the Lord Jesus Christ, etc. You can see what will happen in advance or revisit the past. You can even see what is currently happening hundreds of kilometers from your location. Your contact with the spiritual world can sometimes be only audible. You see nothing but you hear voices that instruct you. All this is quite normal and recognized by the Bible as a channel used by God to direct us:

For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention. In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed; Then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction, that he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man. He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword. (Job 33:14-18) (see also Isaiah 30:20-21)

The discerning of spirits

When our contact with the spiritual world is entirely under the control of the Holy Spirit, the Bible calls this the discerning of spirits (1 Corinthians 12:10). We must humbly ask the Holy Spirit for this gift. For without it, our contact with the spiritual world through visions and voices would be dangerous. The devil and his demons are able to give visions and produce voices to deceive or more exactly to hide their misdeed, produce fear and trouble a person’s spirit. Most visions that produce fear and are not accompanied by any encouragement from the Holy Spirit are of demonic origin and should not be taken literally.

How to react to troubling visions

When your spirit has this kind of contact with the spiritual world, you must react by proclaiming the Word of God and invoking the blood of Jesus Christ to destroy the works of the evil one.

Take the time to calm yourself and clearly recall your vision. Do not let fear dominate you. Remember the words of our God: Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you. (Luke 10:19) no evil shall happen to you, neither shall any plague come near your dwelling. For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways. They will bear you up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot against a stone. (Ps 91:10-12)

Cancel the evil predictions of these visions by the Blood of Jesus Christ. Examine the images with the Word of God, never with the ideas of the world: For Yahweh spoke this to me with a strong hand, and instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying, “Don’t say, ‘A conspiracy!’ concerning all about which this people say, ‘A conspiracy!’ neither fear their threats, nor be terrorized. Yahweh of Armies is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must fear. He is the one you must dread. (Isa 8:11-13) Repent where necessary and take consequent actions.

Safeguards and recommendations

Avoid at all costs forming a doctrine on visions or voices you hear. Everything must line up with the Word of God or be rejected.

Finally, do not force yourself to see or hear in the spiritual world. It is not a necessity. Seeking supernatural visions and voices opens people to demonic manipulations. You can be in control of your spiritual environment without ever having a single vision or hearing a voice that is beyond the senses. The key is to walk by faith and not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7).

Think, speak and act on the Word of God (the truth of the Bible) and you will always be master. For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith. Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? (1 John 5:4-5) So faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. (Rom 10:17)

We live in two dimensions at the same time: physical and spiritual. Man can be in control of his spiritual environment — or be subject to it. The Builder chooses to be in control.

“Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you.” (Luke 10:19)

Who is who

The actors who confront each other

God (John 4:24; Heb 12:9): Father of spirits. Creator of everything. Omnipotent, omniscient, omnipresent. His Word is exalted above everything. He is the sovereign — no spirit can violate his will with impunity.

Man (1 Thess 5:23): Tripartite spirit (spirit, soul, body). Already connected to the spiritual world. In Christ: secure, indestructible connection. The soul and the body can suspend the enjoyment of this connection.

The Devil (1 John 5:19; Eph 2:2): Prince of this world, but NOT omniscient, NOT omnipotent, NOT omnipresent. Controls only the sons of rebellion. A Christian who believes can resist him. His power: already broken by the cross.

Demons (Luke 10:19; 1 John 5:4): Fallen angels under Satan’s orders. Classified into dominions, authorities, powers, evil spirits. All under our feet in Christ. Attracted by idolatry, sexual immorality, hatred.

The actors who serve us

Angels (Heb 1:14; Ps 91:11): Spirits in the service of God and God’s children. Innumerable, organized in ranks (archangels, cherubim, seraphim...). Attracted by praise and holiness. Do not receive worship.

Jesus Christ (Col 2:15; Phil 2:9-10): Supreme chief. Stripped the dominions and authorities. Name above every name. His blood is the impassable limit to the devil. In him: total and assured victory.

The Holy Spirit (John 14:16; 1 Cor 6:17): The connector. Unites his spirit with our spirit at the new birth. Maintains our connection to the spiritual world of light. His presence creates an atmosphere that demons flee.

The limits of the devil: stop overestimating him

✕ NOT omniscient: He does not know the future. He does not know what is happening everywhere. He does not know the thoughts of God’s children.

✕ NOT omnipotent: The blood of Jesus is an impassable limit. The name of Jesus in the mouth of a believer — the devil packs his bags.

✕ NOT omnipresent: He cannot be everywhere at once. He has agents but remains limited in space.

Every Christian who believes in Christ can resist the devil. His power is already broken by the cross (Colossians 2:14-15). You do not have to be afraid.

How to keep your spiritual environment under control

It is your daily practices that determine the level of spiritual influence in your environment:

What attracts angels and the presence of God

• Praise and worship aloud

• Reading and meditating on the Bible

• Regular prayer and fasting

• A life of sanctification and righteousness

• Christian worship music

• Fellowship with sincere believers

What attracts demons and closes the connection

• Idols, fetishes, occult objects

• Profane and fetish music

• Magic/occult movies and series

• Sexual immorality, lust, orgies

• Hatred, quarreling, an atmosphere of war

• Literature of sects and false cults

Angels: their role in your life

Every believer in Christ has a troop of angels who take care of him directly. These angels constantly have access to the presence of God. Here is what you need to know:

What angels do for you

• Watch over your safety (Ps 91:11-12)

• Accompany you in ministry (Heb 1:14)

• Carry out the orders of the Word of God

• Work in your interest when you pray

• Present in atmospheres of praise

What angels do not do

• They do not receive worship — they refuse it!

• They do not work for unbelievers

• You cannot command them at will

• They do not speak to humans of their own accord

• Never invoke angels — it is idolatry

objectifs: You are no longer afraid of the spiritual world — you know who is who and who is in command.
You know the limits of the devil and you stop overestimating him.
You know how to keep your spiritual environment under control.
You live in the full awareness that you are an ambassador of the King who reigns.
